rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act good cause requirement
rules.requirement: A residential landlord may not evict a tenant or fail to renew a written or oral lease without good cause, and must be able to prove the grounds in court. Each cause except nonpayment of rent must be described in detail in a written notice, and a Notice to Quit is required for all good cause evictions except nonpayment of rent.
rules.coverage_text: Most residential rental properties, including single-family homes, mobile homes and land in a mobile home park, apartment buildings, complexes, and rooming and boarding homes. Hotel and motel guests are covered if the occupant has no alternate residence and resides there on a continual basis.
rules.exemptions: May not apply to two- or three-unit owner-occupied premises with two or fewer rental units. Does not apply to hotel guests, motel guests, or guest houses rented to a transient guest or seasonal tenant. Does not apply to a unit held in trust on behalf of an immediate family member who is developmentally disabled and permanently occupies the unit.
rules.quoted_span: No residential landlord may evict or fail to renew a lease, whether it is a written or an oral lease without good cause.

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act: failure to pay rent
rules.requirement: A landlord may take legal action to evict for nonpayment of rent without prior notice, except that a 14-day notice is required before filing if the tenant resides in federally subsidized housing. A tenant may not be evicted for nonpayment if the unpaid rent was used to continue utility services (electric, gas, water, sewer) that the landlord was responsible for and failed to pay.
rules.coverage_text: Residential tenancies covered by the Anti-Eviction Act.
rules.quoted_span: The landlord is not required to give the tenant notice before filing an eviction suit, except if the tenant resides in federally subsidized housing.

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act: disorderly conduct
rules.requirement: A landlord may file for eviction if, after a written Notice to Cease, the tenant continues disorderly conduct that destroys the peace and quiet of other tenants or the neighborhood. A Notice to Quit must be served at least three days before filing.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least three days prior to filing
rules.coverage_text: Residential tenancies covered by the Anti-Eviction Act.
rules.quoted_span: If after given written Notice to Cease disorderly conduct, the tenant continues the disorderly conduct and that conduct destroys the peace and quiet of the other tenants living in the building or neighborhood, the landlord may file a suite for eviction.

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act: damage or destruction to the property
rules.requirement: A tenant may be evicted for intentionally or through gross negligence causing or allowing destruction, damage, or injury to the property. A Notice to Quit must be served at least three days before filing.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least three days prior to filing
rules.coverage_text: Residential tenancies covered by the Anti-Eviction Act.
rules.quoted_span: The tenant may be evicted if they have intentionally or by reason of gross negligence caused or allowed destruction, damage, or injury to the property.

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act: substantial violation of landlord's rules and regulations
rules.requirement: After a written Notice to Cease, a landlord may file for eviction if the tenant continues to substantially violate reasonable rules in the lease or accepted in writing. A Notice to Quit must be served at least one month before filing, given on or before the start of a new month.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least one month prior to filing
rules.coverage_text: Residential tenancies covered by the Anti-Eviction Act.
rules.quoted_span: A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least one month prior to filing the suit for eviction. In addition, any notices must be given on or before the start of a new month (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(d)).
